messages.text: A and I both want the trailer in the next few weeks, and neither of us is backing down. B's pad is where it lives, so she is stuck in the middle. Can you help the three of us sort this out?

I don’t need the trailer. It would be better for me if the pad were clear, but I don’t have a fixed date to give. I rent, and my landlord would need to approve a change to what’s kept there; I haven’t asked him, so I can’t promise anything about the pad yet.

Please give me notice before anyone comes for the trailer, and agree on pickup and return times in advance. I’d prefer visits not be late, and for access to the house to stay clear. I don’t want to referee A and C’s bookings—please arrange those directly and just let me know what affects the pad. I don’t have a towing or storage plan to offer. I’m fine with your draft NCE; please add that landlord approval for the pad hasn’t been checked.

My need is to haul materials for my home project within the next few weeks. The timing window is fixed; the specific dates and times can move, but I won’t simply wait until A is finished. I meant “neither of us is backing down” as: we both need the trailer soon, so we need a fair split or fallback—not that I refuse to compromise.

Working at the same company means requests should use the same process, without workplace pressure or favors. I don’t have dates or times yet for booking, pad clearance, pickup, or return; I also haven’t worked out the shortest usable block or towing and storage details. I’m not sure about specific safety, access, or quiet concerns yet.

I have no objection to checking a plan with all three of us before treating it as settled. Please don’t make B the referee just because the trailer is on B’s pad; I can’t decide the process for everyone.

My NCE: I want the freedom to use the trailer for weekend trips soon. That purpose is fixed; I don’t have exact dates or a firm deadline beyond settling this within the next few weeks. I can’t give pickup/return times, pad-clear dates, towing/storage plans, or a shortest workable block until I choose a weekend and we sort out logistics. I don’t know yet what happens if a date moves.

Working with C shouldn’t add pressure. I want requests handled directly and the plan checked with all three of us before it’s treated as settled. Your draft is fine as a draft; add my need to use it soon, but don’t treat that as agreement to any particular booking.

You recorded my items correctly. I don’t disagree with keeping unknowns visible or with not making me referee. I can’t give a notice period or pickup hours yet, so please leave those unknown; I haven’t asked my landlord about the pad. I’d still prefer it clear, but I can’t promise when that might be.

Your summary of my NCEs is accurate. Add that no booking should be treated as agreed until the three of us confirm it. I agree with your draft judgments. I can’t give exact start/end dates or a workable block yet; my need remains within the next few weeks, and I won’t default to waiting until A is done. I’ll contact A directly about dates.

My need is freedom to use the trailer for weekend trips within the next few weeks. The purpose and that window are fixed; I haven’t picked dates, so I can’t give times, a shortest block, or pickup/return and towing plans yet. No pad-clear date is set. If dates overlap, I suggest splitting the usable time fairly rather than giving the whole period to whoever asked first; fallback details need the dates and logistics. I don’t need special treatment because C and I work together, and I don’t know whether either of us manages the other. I don’t disagree with your NCEs or draft judgments. Add my need and keep the unknowns marked as unknown.

I agree with the new NCEs as draft items, and “change to what is kept there” is clear enough to mean a change to what’s on the pad. I don’t disagree with the plan as a draft, but please don’t treat my silence or check of pad details as permission: I haven’t asked my landlord, and I still can’t give pad timing, notice, or pickup hours. I’d prefer the pad clear, but I don’t want to referee A and C’s bookings.

My NCEs are recorded correctly. I agree with your new NCEs and the plan’s safeguards, including no booking until all three confirm. Change the plan so unknowns stay visible but don’t become an indefinite reason to defer my request; I won’t default to waiting for A. I don’t have dates, a shortest workable block, or a firm start and end date yet. I’ll contact A directly. I don’t know whether either of us manages the other.

I don’t disagree with the new NCEs about pad approval, tow and return details, a written fallback, or keeping work pressure out. I do disagree with requiring B to confirm A and C’s booking; B should confirm pad-related terms, while A and C confirm dates, or B becomes the gatekeeper. I’ll contact C directly, but I have no dates or times yet—my weekend-trip purpose and next-few-weeks window still stand. I don’t know whether either of us manages the other at work. Keep the unknowns listed.

I’m fine with a shared check date, even while my pad details remain unknown, but I don’t have a date to suggest. Please keep clear that my check isn’t permission to use the pad. I’d still rather the trailer not stay in my way, though I know I went along with the arrangement.

I agree with the revised plan and added NCEs, including one shared check date; it must not count as booking or pad permission. I don’t have a specific date to propose yet. I still won’t default to waiting for A. I’ll contact A directly about dates.
